cues: Valence bond theory gives shapes, but not colours or magnetism.
It treats the ligands as point negative charges.
In a free ion all five d orbitals have the same energy.
When ligands approach, they repel the d electrons, and orbitals that point straight at the ligands are pushed up the most.
text: Valence bond theory gives shapes, but not colours or magnetism. Crystal field theory does both. It treats the ligands as point negative charges. In a free ion all five d orbitals have the same energy. When ligands approach, they repel the d electrons, and orbitals that point straight at the ligands are pushed up the most.
